one_line_contribution: A matched-cost break-even measurement: how many self-collection episodes an ALFWorld reader needs before its own success-filtered retrieval pool matches the in-context benefit of a foreign pool (expert walkthroughs or another 32B backbone's successes), with a per-type coverage account (k=3 retrieval saturates at ~3 same-type items, so B*_t ~ m/(p_t f_t)) offered as the explanation.
closest_prior_work: Verified via s2cli (S2 channel): arxiv:2505.00234, 'Self-Generated In-Context Examples Improve LLM Agents for Sequential Decision-Making Tasks' (NeurIPS 2025, 19 cites) — Traj-Bootstrap builds a retrieval database from the agent's OWN successful trajectories on ALFWorld and studies how performance scales as the database grows. It already establishes that a self-collected success pool is a strong in-context memory on this exact environment and that returns to database size flatten, which is most of what P1 would 'discover'. It does not run the matched-collection-cost comparison against a foreign writer's pool, does not report a break-even budget B*, and does not decompose saturation per task type, so it is not a collision — but it is the paper that shrinks the surprise value of the headline, and the proposal never cites it. Also relevant and verified: arxiv:2608.07169 (Agent Memory Distillation, teacher memory to small students, no self-pool control) and arxiv:2512.02543 (In-Context Distillation with Self-Consistency Cascades, ALFWorld cost-accuracy Pareto with a stronger teacher's demonstrations, no self-pool arm) — the proposal characterizes both accurately. arxiv:2604.14004, 2606.19911, 2603.18272 and 2310.17303 also verified and correctly described; I could not find any ID in the proposal that failed verification.
strongest_objection: Four of the five predictions (P1, P2, P3, P5) are equivalence claims whose confirmation is the default outcome of an underpowered design. The stated falsifier is always 'the gap is at least 8 net AND the paired CI excludes 0' — that is not an equivalence test, it is a failed superiority test, so the study confirms 'the self pool catches up at 10%' whenever it lacks the power to show it does not. No TOST, no requirement that the difference CI lie inside +/-8. Worse, the margin is mis-anchored: the brief binds predictions about the retrieval residual to the measured k3-static3 = +17.2 net (CI half-width ~5), but the proposal sets its margins as '30% of the +27 Measurement A effect'. Against the binding +17.2, an 8-net margin is 47% of the entire effect being studied — larger than the whole k1-static3 gain (+9.1). A self pool at b=10% that retained only half the retrieval residual would be reported as 'break-even reached at 10%'. Layered on this, the arm the proposal itself designates as confirmatory for the mechanism, P2, is close to arithmetically entailed: with k=3 and type-conditioned retrieval, capping the bank at m=3 same-type items per type cannot remove any item the reader would have been shown, so the item-count channel the prediction calls 'saturation' is fixed by construction and only within-type match quality can move it — and no arm separates that channel. Meanwhile P4, the only prediction that actually tests the quantitative model m/(p_t f_t), is unresolvable: rho over six per-type points from ~45-game cells cannot separate 0.6 from 0.2, and the stated pooling 'over both draws, both readers and both k' does not exist in the cell list, since b=2.5% cells are run only for the Qwen3 reader at k=3. So the mechanism claim is either tautological (P2) or untestable (P4), and the headline is a default-confirm (P1).
what_would_fix_it: (1) Convert P1/P3/P5 to two-one-sided-tests with a margin strictly smaller than the resolvable difference and anchored to the binding +17.2 residual over static3 — e.g. declare break-even only when the paired-difference CI lies entirely within +/-5, and pre-register 'inconclusive' as a third outcome rather than folding low power into confirmation. (2) Make the coverage arm non-trivial by crossing m with retrieval depth (m=3 at k=7, m=3 vs m=all at k=1) and by adding an m=3 cell that retains the three WORST-matched same-type items, so item count is separable from item quality. (3) Either power P4 or drop it: add b=2.5% cells for the EXAONE reader and for k=1, and replace the Spearman threshold with a per-type regression of deficit on 1/(p_t f_t) with a stated MDE; alternatively pre-commit to the two extreme types (heat vs pick-and-place) as a single planned contrast with an actual power calculation. (4) Match the foreign and self banks on same-type item count, not only on attempted-game index, since the mechanism is about item counts (see missing baseline). (5) Cite and position against 2505.00234, and state what the break-even number adds beyond its database-growth curves. (6) Pre-declare the EXAONE-vs-gpt-oss-120b fallback consequence: a 120B fallback destroys the symmetry premise of P5, which should then be restated as a directional capability-gap prediction rather than a substitution-within-noise claim.
missing_baseline: An item-count-matched foreign pool. The design matches the expert and self pools on attempted train games (the collection-cost axis), but the expert pool covers 1,465 of 3,553 tasks while the self pool yields 1,892 successes from the same 3,553, and both are type-skewed differently (self pool: heat 0.26, pick-and-place 0.81). At any budget b the two banks therefore hold different numbers of same-type items per type — which is precisely the variable the proposal's own saturation mechanism says controls the gain. P3's 'expert vs self at full budget' and the whole budget axis thus confound writer identity with per-type item count, and the retained-gain ratio of at most 1.3 could be produced by coverage alone. A reviewer will demand an expert arm subsampled to the same per-type item counts as the self pool at each budget (and the reverse), which the plan does not include. Secondary omission: a self pool that is NOT success-filtered at the same collection cost (failed episodes included or relabelled), which is the arm that separates 'collection budget' from 'successes per budget' and is the natural companion to 2606.24428's self-confirmation concern.
preprint_collision: No verified collision. The proposal's own check is unusually good for this pipeline: three classed queries with channels, IDs, and stated outcomes, plus two IDs verified through s2cli paper (2512.02543, 2603.18272). I re-ran it and extended it. Queries (all channel (a), the s2cli S2+HF command; channel (b) WebSearch was unavailable this session and was not used): Q1 'break-even budget self-collected experience versus expert demonstrations in-context agent memory' --recent -> MemHarness 2607.28272, SelfMem 2607.03726, AutoMem 2607.01224, RaMem 2606.22844, LongMemEval-V2 2605.12493, MemoryArena 2602.16313; none compares a self pool to a foreign pool at matched cost. Q2 'how many in-context demonstrations saturate retrieval few-shot exemplar budget diminishing returns coverage' -> FewMMBench 2602.21854, gradient-matching demo selection 2506.04579, long-context ICL 2405.00200 (gains come from attention to similar examples, not cumulative learning) — the closest thing to a saturation claim, but for classification ICL, not agent experience pools. Q3 (closest named method) 'Agent Memory Distillation teacher trajectories hierarchical memory student agent without training' -> 2608.07169 verified (no self-pool control), DuoMem 2606.29961, HiPS 2608.25329, FORGE 2605.16233, OPD-Evolver 2606.17628; none runs the reader's own pool at matched collection cost. Q4 'matched cost comparison foreign experience pool versus agent own collected trajectories ALFWorld retrieval' --recent -> Auto-Dreamer 2605.20616, Evolving-RL 2605.10663, ProactAgent 2604.20572, and critically arxiv:2505.00234 (verified: NeurIPS 2025, 19 cites, self-generated in-context examples on ALFWorld) — the proposal's check missed this one entirely, and it is the paper closest to the self-pool half of the design. Q5 'experience bank size ablation number of stored trajectories diminishing returns memory augmented LLM agent' -> 2608.15008, 2606.24775, 2606.06448, 2604.03295, 2603.04549; bank-size and admission work exists but none reports a per-type coverage break-even. Q6 'when does teacher demonstration advantage vanish student self-collected data amortized cost shared memory' --recent -> 2608.07169, 2608.00017 (memory reward inflation), 2602.05965; empty on the central claim. Verified IDs: 2608.07169, 2604.14004, 2606.19911, 2512.02543, 2603.18272, 2310.17303, 2606.24428, 2505.00234 — all exist and match the descriptions given; none failed verification. So the break-even estimand itself appears unclaimed, and I score novelty on that; the deduction is for the missed 2505.00234, which makes the self-pool arm a re-run of a published method the proposal does not name, and for the fact that the saturation half of the claim is anticipated in spirit by existing database-growth and bank-size ablations.
